# dsh-plugins
English · 中文

Plugins for **DSH** (DeepSeek Harness) — and the notes I wish I had
when writing the first one.
| Plugin | What it does |
| `plugins/deepseek-web-chat` | A chat.deepseek.com panel in DSH's right sidebar: ask the web chat f
rom inside the app, with workspace files or a DSH conversation attached as context. Uses your own ac
count, no API key. |
## Why a repo for plugins

A DSH plugin is small but not obvious: it has a **Host half** (a Cordis plugin that owns services,
H

TTP routes and credentials) and a **browser half** (a bundle the DSH web UI registers as a slot),
pl
us a bundle patch so the loader knows the Host row. This repo keeps those pieces in one place with a
repeatable layout, tests and a reload workflow:

## Quick start
Open **Plugins → Add plugin** in DSH and paste this one line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DSH installs it with pnpm and enables it as a bundle; refresh the page (restart once if the sidebar
tab is missing) and open **DeepSeek Chat** from the `+` menu. The proof-of-work module is fetched on
first use, so there is nothing else to download.

Prefer a local checkout (for development)? `git clone` the repo and follow
`plugins/deepseek-web-cha

t/README.md` (English) or
`README.zh-CN.md` (中文).
## Reading order

1. `docs/writing-a-plugin.md` — Host half, browser half, bundle patch,
the module-cache trick that m

akes hot reload work, and the testing pyramid this repo follows.
2. `plugins/deepseek-web-chat` — a

complete worked example: credentials,
an HTTP route, an SSE stream, a WebAssembly dependency, drag-a

nd-drop context, bilingual UI.
3. `plugins/deepseek-web-chat/docs/guide.en.md` — the
user-facing gui

drop context, bilingual UI.
3. `plugins/deepseek-web-chat/docs/guide.en.md` — the
user-facing guide.
## Conventions

- **One plugin per directory** under `plugins/`, named after its package (`dsh-<name>`).
- **Bilingu

al docs**: every human-facing document exists as `X.md` (English) and `X.zh-CN.md`
(中文), each starti

ng with a language switcher line.
- **No personal data in git**: no absolute home paths, no account

identifiers, no tokens, no
screenshots of a real account. See the checklist in the writing guide.
-

**Downloaded assets stay out**: vendor blobs (like the proof-of-work module) are fetched by a
script
and listed in `.gitignore`.
## Privacy
These plugins run inside your DSH and talk to third-party services with **your** credentials. Nothin

g
is collected by this repository: there is no telemetry, and no server of mine is involved. Each
pl

ugin's README has a *Privacy* section that states exactly what it stores and what leaves your
machin
e — read it before attaching files or conversations as context.
